decisions.executionNote: Raise the right wrist and progressively orient the open gripper downward toward the basket, maintaining a continuous elbow-up approach.
Advance above the near-left part of the basket while continuing the downward wrist rotation; keep fingers open and clear of the eggs.
Align the right gripper over the near-left egg with a vertical approach, descending only to a pre-grasp height.
Make a small visual centering correction and lower the open fingers around the near-left egg.
Close around the centered near-left egg, then lift slowly to check retention visually.
The egg is not retained. Reopen and recenter over the displaced near egg, with a slightly rearward approach before lowering again.
Close slowly around the visually centered near egg at the present depth, then test retention with a small vertical lift.
Lift the egg clear of the basket with the gripper commanded closed, checking that it stays between the fingers before transfer.
The egg remains visibly held. Carry it toward the holder above the basket rim, with the left arm stationary and right fingers closed.
Retention is uncertain: the egg appears below the closed fingers. Reopen and approach the egg just left of the basket for a deeper centered grasp.
The dropped egg has rolled toward the holder. Follow its observed position and descend with open fingers to recover it from the tabletop.
Replan from the actual wrist pose with smaller motions, moving away from the basket and centering the fingers over the isolated egg.
Tracking suggests contact or obstruction near the basket. Withdraw upward and rearward before making another approach to the isolated egg.
With clearance regained, move above the isolated egg and restore a near-vertical gripper orientation for a centered tabletop grasp.
Lower vertically over the stationary isolated egg, keeping the open gripper clear of the basket and monitoring its centering.
Descend the final short distance around the isolated egg, with a small lateral centering correction before closing.
The egg is centered between the fingers at tabletop depth. Close without further downward motion and let the grasp settle before lifting.
Lift the centered egg straight up with the gripper kept closed, checking visually for stable retention before transferring.
Retention failed during the lift. Reopen and approach farther forward and deeper around the egg's equator rather than its tapered upper surface.
Adjust the open fingers slightly forward so their contact surfaces straddle the egg more deeply, then close gradually without lifting.
Finish closing at the deeper contact location, pause to settle, and make a short test lift while keeping the gripper closed.
The egg slipped out again. Reopen and lower the contact surfaces farther toward the egg's equator, correcting the fore-aft alignment before another grasp.
Relieve the downward contact and correct the grasp center leftward and rearward using the head view rather than assuming the wrist image center is the pinch point.
Correct the wrist tilt and lateral alignment over the egg while staying clear of the tabletop; use the resulting finger-to-egg view to set the pinch.
Bring the egg's equator into the finger contact region with a small forward and downward adjustment, then close at a fixed pose.
Transfer the centered egg toward the nearest holder cup with a low, gently rising motion and closed fingers; retention remains uncertain.
Open and lift clear of the holder to locate the egg and inspect the cups before selecting the next grasp.
Approach the leftmost remaining basket egg from above with a slightly oblique gripper orientation, keeping clearance from the basket rim.
Lower the oblique open gripper toward the leftmost basket egg, with a small forward alignment correction.
Complete the slow descent around the leftmost egg, keeping the oblique wrist orientation and open fingers.
Close around the egg with a small centering correction, then lift rearward out of the basket while keeping the gripper closed.
The egg slipped back into the basket. Reopen, lift clear, and change to a diagonal side-biased pinch to avoid squeezing its upper tapered surface.
Approach the nearest basket egg with the diagonal gripper, descending gradually while monitoring clearance and centering.
Lower the diagonal fingers another short distance around the nearest egg, keeping its center between the open jaws.
Close the diagonal pinch gradually at a fixed wrist pose and let the egg settle before testing a lift.
The egg sits off-center in the pinch. Reopen and shift the diagonal jaws rightward and rearward, then close around a deeper contact region.
Lift briefly with closed fingers to clear the rim and determine whether the egg is retained or has been displaced.
Reopen and advance the diagonal gripper toward the egg that moved forward in the basket, using a shallow approach to avoid another off-center pinch.
Lower the open diagonal pinch over the central egg with a small rightward correction, aiming for contact around its widest section.
Close the now-centered diagonal pinch, pause, and make a short vertical retention test without changing orientation.
Raise the centered pinch vertically with the fingers closed to verify retention clear of the basket.
The egg remains in the basket. Reopen and descend to a deeper side contact with a small leftward correction rather than repeating the shallow pinch.
Relieve contact with the basket and reposition the open jaws rearward so the egg lies nearer the useful fingertip contact area.
Use the clearer view to center the egg between the diagonal fingertips, close at a fixed pose, and make only a short test lift.
Lift the egg clear with closed fingers and begin a slow leftward transfer, checking whether it remains between the jaws.
Retention failed. Recenter using the head projection of the middle egg, approaching farther right and lower with open diagonal jaws.
Lower around the middle egg at the corrected lateral position, keeping the fingers fully open until the contact depth is visible.
Center the egg along the diagonal jaw axis, close gradually around its widest section, and start a small upward retention test.
Lift the closed pinch up and slightly rearward to clear the basket; verify whether the egg follows before proceeding to the holder.
The egg now appears retained above the basket. Carry it leftward with closed fingers and additional rim clearance, preserving the grasp orientation.
Continue carrying the visibly retained egg toward the holder at a clear height, keeping the right gripper closed and its orientation fixed.
Lower the retained egg toward the front-right holder cup, correcting leftward while preserving the diagonal grasp.
The egg appears to have settled into the holder. Open the fingers and withdraw upward to inspect its placement without disturbing it.
One egg is visible in the back-right holder cup. Return above the basket with open fingers to collect another egg, maintaining the diagonal grasp orientation.
Approach above the nearer remaining basket egg with the open diagonal gripper, leaving clearance for a final visual alignment.
Lower toward the nearer egg while making a small rightward and forward centering correction, keeping the jaws open.
Close around the centered near egg at the observed depth, then start a short upward and rearward retention test.
The egg is still in the basket. Reopen and advance the jaws farther around its equator before closing, rather than repeating the shallow pinch.
Correct the lateral offset while preserving the deeper fore-aft engagement, then close the centered pinch at a fixed pose.
Lift the deeper pinch upward and slightly rearward with closed fingers, checking whether the egg follows clear of the basket.
Reopen and approach the near egg at a lower contact height, with a small lateral correction; previous pinches have slipped from its upper surface.
At the deeper contact height, shift the pinch rearward along the egg and close, then begin a short lift to check retention.
Lift the now-centered egg upward and slightly rearward with closed fingers, preserving the grasp orientation and checking retention above the basket.
The egg is visibly retained. Carry it toward the holder with closed fingers and lift enough to clear the basket rim.
The egg slipped during transfer. Reopen above the basket and change to a vertical approach over its new position, avoiding the slanted pinch that expelled it.
Descend vertically toward the near egg, correcting slightly rightward and forward while keeping the jaws open.
Lower the vertical fingers to the egg's equator with a small lateral correction, close, and begin a short straight lift.
The egg lies behind the useful pinch region. Reopen and move the wrist rearward at the current depth to center it between the fingertip pads.
Close the newly centered pinch and lift clear promptly, starting a smooth leftward transfer only after gaining rim clearance.
The egg remains between the fingers after lifting. Carry it smoothly toward the empty front-right cup with a fixed wrist orientation and closed gripper.
The egg is retained. Align its observed offset with the empty front-right cup and lower smoothly, keeping the gripper closed until seated.
